rationale: Clinical characterization from the index kindreds described by Torella et al. (12 affected individuals with p.Glu415Lys) demonstrates full penetrance of oculomotor abnormalities (nystagmus in 12/12, 100%, and broken smooth pursuit), while dysarthria was explicitly described as only 'sometimes' present. The expansion study by Benkirane et al. (12 additional cases across varied TUBA4A missense alleles) corroborated that ophthalmological examination consistently reveals nystagmus or abnormal ocular movements across patients presenting with spasticity and/or ataxia. However, while available sources uniformly highlight prominent ocular motor abnormalities as primary signs and speech impairment/dysarthria as an inconsistent finding, precise pooled quantitative percentages across the full multicentric Benkirane cohort are truncated in the available text extracts.

evidence.text: Torella et al. identified a novel TUBA4A missense mutation (p.Glu415Lys) in two families comprising 12 affected individuals presenting with spastic ataxia. All evaluated patients demonstrated ocular motor abnormalities (nystagmus and broken smooth pursuit), while dysarthria occurred only sometimes.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact frequency and breakdown of cerebellar dysarthria versus specific oculomotor signs across all non-p.Glu415Lys TUBA4A missense variants in the Benkirane et al. cohort?
new_directions.rationale: While Torella et al. report 100% nystagmus and infrequent dysarthria for p.Glu415Lys, examining whether allele-specific differences exist across other TUBA4A variants is needed to solidify the penetrance threshold.

new_directions.question_text: Can quantitative video-oculography differentiate TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia from other early-stage autosomal dominant spastic ataxias such as SPAX/HSP phenocopies?
new_directions.rationale: Since ocular signs like nystagmus and broken pursuit occur early and with high penetrance, objective oculometric biomarkers could serve as a sensitive clinical discriminator.
